blocking.problem:
Oracle calls have implicit writes to tgt/fr, but transfer constructs writes only from row.lhs and lift.perm_call mutable operands. Its assumption that all oracle XOR deliveries commute misses a delivery into another outstanding invocation's input. Reproduced a memoryless object (ptr_width=32), oracle i with in=[8],tgt=8,fault=4,args=[], and oracle o with in=[],tgt=8,fault=4,args=[token]. Bodies:
oracle @i (x:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()
^entry():
lift.retval x
oracle @o () (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () (tk:token)
regs { a:reg[8], b:reg[8], r:reg[8], fr:reg[4], fr2:reg[4] }
^entry():
a = lift.const.i8 1
b = lift.const.i8 2
lift.oracle_call @i tk (a) r fr () ()
lift.oracle_call @i tk (b) a fr2 () ()
lift.oracle_uncall @i tk (a) r fr () ()
lift.retval r
After rehashing, check exits 0/status ok; run-oracle /dev/stdin o --input "" --budget 6 --arg token:1,0,0,0 returns {code:0,payload:2,steps:6}; step-check --exhaustive with those options also returns ok (one case). Hand trace: first r=1, intervening call changes a=1 XOR 2=3, then uncall changes r=1 XOR 3=2. The required unchanged input is violated, so the object must never reach execution.
blocking.fix: Change src/call_discipline.rs::validate_matched_oracle_calls transfer to include implicit target and fault writes of both lift.oracle_call and lift.oracle_uncall when invalidating other outstanding invocations whose ins intersect those locations. Clear address-constant knowledge for those destinations too. Preserve the legitimate commuting shared-output/multiplicity cases: distinguish writes to an outstanding input from XOR updates to its target/fault. §5.5 requires "same token, callee, ins and mem values (no intervening row writes those locations or cells: suite F)"; §4.2 explicitly writes "tgt ^= payload; fr ^= code". Expected: the exact object above is rejected at parse/check with §5.5 (CLI exit 1, empty stdout). Add it to tests/r1_rules.rs and a variant where another invocation's fault destination writes a tracked input. Positive: remove the middle call, use outer B=5 and token B=1; require payload=0,code=0,steps=5 and complete prefix reversal. Keep two-call/two-uncall positives.

blocking.problem:
The exchange fix can be bypassed by putting the exchange inside a permutation action. Region-call transfer reads only ins and in-regions, omitting mutable bundles and mutable regions; it updates outputs separately. Reproduced memoryless signatures: c kind=perm_action,mut=[1,1],in=[],mem=[],args=[],bounds=[]; a kind=action with the same widths. Bodies:
perm_action @c (a:wire mut, b:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
swap a b
action @a (t:wire mut, m:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
d = qalloc any 1
h d
action_call @c (d, m) () () ()
cx m t
adj action_call @c (d, m) () () ()
h d
qfree d
Rehashed check exits 0/status ok. run-action /dev/stdin a --mut 0,0 exits 1 with §4.3 E_QREG_NOT_CLEAN, an exactly nonzero [false,false,true] component of amplitude 0.5. Hand trace: H(d), SWAP(d,m), CX(m,t), SWAP(d,m) entangles d with t; final H(d) does not clean d. Replacing child swap with cx a b yields the same accepted dirty-release failure. Doubling the middle cx m t is accepted and executes as identity, state {"00":[1,0]}. Direct versions of this class now reject, so validation depends unsoundly on a call boundary.
blocking.fix: Change src/validation.rs::validate_action_sequence's action_call/adj/ctl transfer and Discipline to snapshot all old mut, ins and region-cell dependencies before changing any output, propagate their union to every mut bundle/cell, and retain transitive readers of those values across a call and its adjoint. Joint inverses must bind entry versions and cancel all participating outputs consistently, as the exchange fix already does. §6.1 specifies "each mut: perm with S = mut ∪ ins ∪ cells(regions passed) ∪ Π" and the same S for mut-region cells; §6.2 binds cleanup to its "exact computing sequence"; §6.3 requires factorisation from remaining state. Expected: both quoted swap-child and CX-child negatives reject at load citing §6.2. Add them to tests/r1_discipline.rs, together with a mut-region transfer analogue. Positive controls doubling the middle CX must parse and execute forward/adjoint on all t,m basis entries and a superposed entry, returning clean workspace and exact entry state after reversal. Extend tests/r1_fuzz_discipline.rs with equivalent direct versus called computations.

blocking.problem:
The borrow compiler hoists child-local regions as Alloc nodes, never appends their function-exit restoration/release, then reverses that incomplete node sequence for an adjoint call. Node::adjoint turns Alloc into Free, so an adjoint-only invocation tries to free a symbolic region that was never allocated. Reproduced a memoryless object, both functions kind=perm_action with mut=[1],in=[],mem=[],args=[],bounds=[]:
perm_action @c (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
qregion r 1 1
x t
x t
perm_action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
b = qborrow any 1
cx b t
adj action_call @c (t) () () ()
cx b t
qreturn b
The hash CLI exits 1: "§5.6: a wire released inside a borrow frame is not clean". Removing only "adj " makes hash exit 0. Hand derivation: c allocates a zero region, performs X twice, restores/releases that unchanged region, so c=c†=I; parent is CX(b,t) I CX(b,t)=I on every t,b, including b entangled with an external system. This is a false rejection of a defined valid program, not an uncertifiable black-box borrow operation.
blocking.fix: In src/borrow.rs compile complete local-region lifetimes for inlined functions: unconditional allocation and image preparation at entry, body in the selected direction, inverse image gates and release at exit. Either reverse the complete entry/body/exit node sequence or keep the lifetime wrapper fixed and reverse only the body; do not reverse a lone Alloc into an unmatched Free. Represent image preparation separately or make lifecycle nodes preserve the image on adjoint, since Node::adjoint currently discards it. §4.6 says "created at function entry" and "back at its image before exit, image gates reversed, cells released clean"; §5.3 includes "qregion creation ↔ release". Expected: the exact object parses; run-action a --mut 0/1 and reverse succeed with the same t and equals_entry=true. Add a tests/r1_borrow.rs regression requiring acceptance and forward/adjoint/exact restoration for every t,b basis value and a borrowed system entangled with a reference. Also cover a nonzero image (e.g. qregion r 1 4 @image, one-byte image ff) and a declaration nested in a zero-trip loop; these must have the same function-entry lifetime in forward and adjoint calls.
